To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calmodulin binds to a C-terminal region in TRPV5 and that calmodulin binding is required for Ca2+-dependent TRPV5 inactivation.
calmodulin binds to a C-terminal peptide of TRPV5, which negatively regulates TRPV5 activity.
calmodulin negatively controls the open probability of TRPV5, whereas PTH reverses this control by inducing phosphorylation of the TRPV5 C-terminal tail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of calmodulin action and modulation by parathyroid hormone on TRPV5.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying Ca2+ and PTH-dependent regulation of TRPV5 activity.
the role of calmoduline and the C terminus of TRPV5 in the regulation of Ca2+ transport in the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calmodulin acts as a brake to limit Ca2+ influx and that PTH removes the brake by phosphorylation of the channel.
calmodulin is a negative regulator of TRPV5 activity and that PTH is a positive regulator of TRPV activity.
PTH stimulates TRPV5 activity through a mechanism in which PKA-mediated phosphorylation of TRPV5 at T709 reduces calmodulin binding and thus prevents Ca2+-dependent channel inactivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+ influx via TRPV5 is negatively regulated by calmodulin and this negative regulation can be reversed by PTH-induced phosphorylation.
calmodulin acts as an endogenous inhibitor of TRPV5 and that PTH reverses this inhibition through a mechanism involving PKA-dependent phosphorylation of TRPV5.
calmodulin is involved in the Ca2+-dependent channel inactivation of TRPV5 and that this inactivation is counteracted by PKA-mediated phosphorylation of T709.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calmodulin is a negative modulator of TRPV5 activity that is relieved by phosphorylation of the channel by PKA, which is induced by PTH.
Ca2+-dependent calmodulin binding is a key mechanism for the inactivation of the Ca2+ channel TRPV5 and that calmodulin binding can be modulated by PTH-induced channel phosphorylation.
the TRPV5 C-terminal tail contains a Ca2+-sensitive binding site for calmodulin that is important for Ca2+ channel inactivation.
